name: CyberForge assistant eval
about: Questions a user asks the desktop AI Assistant, sent to the live ML service exactly as the assistant sends them (streamed, think=auto, history as chat turns).
Each case lists required facts as regular expressions (every group must match, case-insensitive) and forbidden statements (none may match).
These patterns were written for this eval, independently of the reference library's own `required` patterns, so the check is not the service grading itself.

Answers are scored twice: the served answer, and the model's own words (the served answer without any 'From the reviewed sources' supplement; an answer the service replaced with reviewed facts counts as a model failure).
kind: covered = a topic in the reviewed reference library (ref = its id); uncovered = no reference exists, so the model answers unaided; followup = needs the earlier turns; smalltalk = a greeting.
Automatic word patterns are strict; a correct answer phrased differently can fail them. Read failures by hand before calling them wrong.

cases.q: Hi there!
How can I tell if an email is a phishing attempt?
I clicked a link in a suspicious email and typed my password. What should I do now?
My files were encrypted by ransomware. Should I just pay the ransom?
I keep getting MFA push notifications I didn't request. What is happening?
must: deny|reject|decline|don.t approve|do not approve|never approve|not approve|ignore

What is SQL injection and the best way to prevent it?
How do I prevent cross-site scripting in a web app?
What is CSRF and how is it prevented?
Explain server-side request forgery.
Is it safe to scan a QR code on a parking meter that asks me to pay?
A website told me to press Win+R and paste a command to verify I'm human. Is that safe?
What is an infostealer?
What is business email compromise?
I got an email saying they have a video of me and want Bitcoin. What should I do?
I think my email account was hacked. How do I recover it?
What is a zero-day vulnerability?
What do CVE and CVSS mean?
What is a domain generation algorithm used by malware?
What is a DDoS attack?
What is a good backup strategy against ransomware?
What makes a strong password?
If a website has a padlock and HTTPS, does that mean it's safe?
What are SPF, DKIM and DMARC?
What is zero trust security?
must: never trust|no implicit trust|not trusted by default|verif

cases.q: What is an adversary-in-the-middle phishing attack?

history.content: Phishing is a scam where attackers send messages that pretend to be from a trusted organisation to trick you into clicking a link, opening an attachment or giving away passwords.

cases.q: And what about when it comes by text message?

history.content: Credential stuffing uses leaked username and password pairs from one site to try to sign in to other sites, because many people reuse passwords.

cases.q: How do I protect my accounts from it?
What is a SIM swap attack?
What is a software supply chain attack?
What was Log4Shell?
What is DNS tunneling?
Is it safe to use public Wi-Fi for online banking?
